blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 3.35
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 3.35

blocks.text: मोहप्रतिसंहतस्तु कर्मात्मा
blocks.directed: [slowly] मोहप्रतिसंहतस्तु कर्मात्मा

blocks.text: Mohapratisaṃhatas tu karmātmā.
blocks.directed: Mohapratisaṃhatas tu karmātmā.

blocks.text: But the one compacted in delusion is constituted by karmic activity.
blocks.directed: But the one compacted in delusion is constituted by karmic activity.

blocks.text: You’ve Been Doing Karma. Karma Has Been Doing You.
blocks.directed: You’ve Been Doing Karma. Karma Has Been Doing You.

blocks.text: Now this is a wonderful contrast.
blocks.directed: Now this is a wonderful contrast.

blocks.text: And notice that little word again.
blocks.directed: And notice that little word again.

blocks.text: Tu.
blocks.directed: Tu.

blocks.text: But.
blocks.directed: But.

blocks.text: On the one hand, the liberated yogi.
blocks.directed: On the one hand, the liberated yogi.

blocks.text: Kevalī.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Kevalī.

blocks.text: On the other hand, the bound individual.
blocks.directed: On the other hand, the bound individual.

blocks.text: Karmātmā.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Karmātmā.

blocks.text: The one whose identity is bound up with action.
blocks.directed: The one whose identity is bound up with action.

blocks.text: Let’s unpack the Sanskrit.
blocks.directed: Let’s unpack the Sanskrit.

blocks.text: Moha — delusion, bewilderment, ignorance.
blocks.directed: Moha — delusion, bewilderment, ignorance.

blocks.text: Pratisaṃhata — compacted, gathered densely, thoroughly enveloped.
blocks.directed: Pratisaṃhata — compacted, gathered densely, thoroughly enveloped.

blocks.text: Karma — action, deed, karmic activity.
blocks.directed: Karma — action, deed, karmic activity.

blocks.text: Ātmā — self, here the individual understood through involvement in karma.
blocks.directed: Ātmā — self, here the individual understood through involvement in karma.

blocks.text: Now, mohapratisaṃhata is a magnificent word.
blocks.directed: Now, mohapratisaṃhata is a magnificent word.

blocks.text: A compact mass of delusion.
blocks.directed: A compact mass of delusion.

blocks.text: Not merely:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Not merely:

blocks.text: “I happen to be mistaken about one particular thing.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I happen to be mistaken about one particular thing.”

blocks.text: No.
blocks.directed: No.

blocks.text: The whole structure of ordinary self-identification is saturated with misrecognition.
blocks.directed: The whole structure of ordinary self-identification is saturated with misrecognition.

blocks.text: The individual believes themselves to be a finite subject possessing independent agency.
blocks.directed: The individual believes themselves to be a finite subject possessing independent agency.

blocks.text: They experience the world as fundamentally separate.
blocks.directed: They experience the world as fundamentally separate.

blocks.text: They act through attraction and aversion.
blocks.directed: They act through attraction and aversion.

blocks.text: And those actions produce karmic consequences.
blocks.directed: And those actions produce karmic consequences.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja explains that the bound person becomes the receptacle of pleasure and pain precisely because they are enveloped in ignorance.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja explains that the bound person becomes the receptacle of pleasure and pain precisely because they are enveloped in ignorance.

blocks.text: And they are continually implicated in good and bad actions.
blocks.directed: And they are continually implicated in good and bad actions.

blocks.text: Śubha.
blocks.directed: Śubha.

blocks.text: Auspicious, good.
blocks.directed: Auspicious, good.

blocks.text: Aśubha.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Aśubha.

blocks.text: Inauspicious, bad.
blocks.directed: Inauspicious, bad.

blocks.text: Now, here’s something important.
blocks.directed: Now, here’s something important.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja isn’t saying morally good and bad actions are indistinguishable.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja isn’t saying morally good and bad actions are indistinguishable.

blocks.text: Quite the opposite.
blocks.directed: Quite the opposite.

blocks.text: He explicitly discusses their consequences.
blocks.directed: He explicitly discusses their consequences.

blocks.text: But both belong to the condition of the individual agent acting under limited identification.
blocks.directed: But both belong to the condition of the individual agent acting under limited identification.

blocks.text: The person experiences:
blocks.directed: [short pause] The person experiences:

blocks.text: “I am the doer.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I am the doer.”

blocks.text: “I performed this action.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I performed this action.”

blocks.text: “I must receive the result.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I must receive the result.”

blocks.text: And the entire karmic machinery becomes involved.
blocks.directed: And the entire karmic machinery becomes involved.

blocks.text: Now, remember the three malas.
blocks.directed: Now, remember the three malas.

blocks.text: Āṇavamala — the primordial sense of limitation.
blocks.directed: Āṇavamala — the primordial sense of limitation.

blocks.text: Māyīyamala — the experience of differentiation.
blocks.directed: Māyīyamala — the experience of differentiation.

blocks.text: Kārmamala — the limitation associated with agency and karmic action.
blocks.directed: Kārmamala — the limitation associated with agency and karmic action.

blocks.text: Here we’re seeing the consequences of the third.
blocks.directed: Here we’re seeing the consequences of the third.

blocks.text: The individual isn’t merely experiencing a separate world.
blocks.directed: The individual isn’t merely experiencing a separate world.

blocks.text: They are acting within it through the conviction of limited doership.
blocks.directed: They are acting within it through the conviction of limited doership.

blocks.text: And therefore the consequences of action become part of their conditioned existence.
blocks.directed: And therefore the consequences of action become part of their conditioned existence.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja cites the Kālikākrama to explain how ignorance and conceptual construction prevent the individual from recognising the tattvas, beginning with Śiva, as manifestations of consciousness.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja cites the Kālikākrama to explain how ignorance and conceptual construction prevent the individual from recognising the tattvas, beginning with Śiva, as manifestations of consciousness.

blocks.text: Then good and bad conditions arise through the person’s dependence upon ignorance.
blocks.directed: Then good and bad conditions arise through the person’s dependence upon ignorance.

blocks.text: And suffering follows from inauspicious states and deeds. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: And suffering follows from inauspicious states and deeds. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: Now think about the contrast with the previous sūtra.
blocks.directed: Now think about the contrast with the previous sūtra.

blocks.text: The kevalī experiences the body and mind without treating their changing states as the ultimate Self.
blocks.directed: The kevalī experiences the body and mind without treating their changing states as the ultimate Self.

blocks.text: The karmātmā identifies with the limited subject and its actions.
blocks.directed: The karmātmā identifies with the limited subject and its actions.

blocks.text: One recognises the underlying reality.
blocks.directed: One recognises the underlying reality.

blocks.text: The other remains caught within its contracted manifestation.
blocks.directed: The other remains caught within its contracted manifestation.

blocks.text: And the important difference isn’t necessarily visible from the outside.
blocks.directed: And the important difference isn’t necessarily visible from the outside.

blocks.text: Two people might perform the same ordinary action.
blocks.directed: Two people might perform the same ordinary action.

blocks.text: They might both walk down a road.
blocks.directed: They might both walk down a road.

blocks.text: Speak to another person.
blocks.directed: Speak to another person.

blocks.text: Eat a meal.
blocks.directed: Eat a meal.

blocks.text: But Kṣemarāja’s philosophical distinction concerns the conscious standpoint from which action occurs.
blocks.directed: But Kṣemarāja’s philosophical distinction concerns the conscious standpoint from which action occurs.

blocks.text: Not merely the outward movement.
blocks.directed: Not merely the outward movement.

blocks.text: One identifies with the finite agent as ultimate.
blocks.directed: One identifies with the finite agent as ultimate.

blocks.text: The other recognises the universal conscious source.
blocks.directed: The other recognises the universal conscious source.

blocks.text: Of course, this doesn’t remove conventional responsibility.
blocks.directed: Of course, this doesn’t remove conventional responsibility.

blocks.text: A person claiming spiritual liberation cannot simply declare themselves exempt from the consequences of harming others.
blocks.directed: A person claiming spiritual liberation cannot simply declare themselves exempt from the consequences of harming others.

blocks.text: The metaphysical recognition of Śiva is not an ethical loophole.
blocks.directed: The metaphysical recognition of Śiva is not an ethical loophole.

blocks.text: But the tradition’s point is that the ordinary structure of karmic bondage depends upon limited self-identification.
blocks.directed: But the tradition’s point is that the ordinary structure of karmic bondage depends upon limited self-identification.

blocks.text: And now comes the extraordinary turn.
blocks.directed: And now comes the extraordinary turn.

blocks.text: Because even the person compacted in delusion hasn’t ceased to be Śiva in their fundamental nature.
blocks.directed: Because even the person compacted in delusion hasn’t ceased to be Śiva in their fundamental nature.

blocks.text: Which means the possibility of recognition remains.
blocks.directed: Which means the possibility of recognition remains.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja introduces śaktipāta.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja introduces śaktipāta.

blocks.text: The descent of divine grace.
blocks.directed: The descent of divine grace.

blocks.text: The intervention of Śiva’s own power through which the individual’s innate freedom becomes disclosed.
blocks.directed: The intervention of Śiva’s own power through which the individual’s innate freedom becomes disclosed.

blocks.text: And suddenly the whole situation changes.
blocks.directed: And suddenly the whole situation changes.

blocks.text: The compact mass of delusion doesn’t have to remain compact forever.
blocks.directed: The compact mass of delusion doesn’t have to remain compact forever.

blocks.text: The limitation can be recognised.
blocks.directed: The limitation can be recognised.

blocks.text: Difference can be transcended.
blocks.directed: Difference can be transcended.

blocks.text: And then, according to the tradition, something rather spectacular becomes possible.
blocks.directed: And then, according to the tradition, something rather spectacular becomes possible.

blocks.text: The creation of another world.
blocks.directed: The creation of another world.

blocks.text: Oh, for God’s sake.
blocks.directed: Oh, for God’s sake.

blocks.text: We’re back to supernatural powers.
blocks.directed: We’re back to supernatural powers.

blocks.text: Apparently Śiva cannot resist showing off.
blocks.directed: Apparently Śiva cannot resist showing off.
